intro_en: In this lesson you will learn to introduce yourself in Japanese. You will say your name, country, job and age. You will say "I am a student" and "I am not a student". You will also ask "Are you a student?". You will see that Japanese word order is just like Tamil. The main word comes at the end of the sentence. Small words like は come after the noun, as in Tamil. You will also learn the numbers 0 to 10. And you will learn the greetings you will use in class every day.

g01-1.explanation_en: To say "X is Y" in Japanese, use 「N1 は N2 です」. N1 is the first noun and N2 is the second noun. は shows the topic, the thing you are talking about. Here it is read "wa", not "ha". It means "about X…". です ends the sentence in a polite way. It is close to the Tamil "ஆக இருக்கிறார் / இருக்கிறது" (is). Tamil says "நான் மாணவன்" (I [am a] student) with no verb. In the same way, です alone is enough here. Like Tamil, Japanese puts the main word at the end of the sentence. If it is clear who is speaking, you can drop 私は. Tamil speakers do this too.
g01-1.tamil_parallel_en: நான் மாணவன் (ஆக இருக்கிறேன்) "I am a student" = 私は 学生です。 Here は is roughly "நானோ / நான் என்றால்" (as for me). です is roughly "ஆக இருக்கிறேன்" (I am).
g01-1.pitfalls_en: Don’t read は as "ha". When it marks the topic, it is always read "wa". Use です only once in each sentence. If you end with just 「学生」 and no です, it is casual speech. It is not polite.

g01-2.explanation_en: To say "X is not Y", put じゃありません in place of です. It is just like the "இல்லை" (not) at the end of the Tamil "நான் மாணவன் இல்லை / அல்ல" (I am not a student). じゃありません is the spoken form of ではありません. In writing, or in very polite speech, you can also say ではありません. As in Tamil, the "not" comes at the end of the sentence. So you only know if the answer is "yes" or "no" after you hear the whole sentence.
g01-2.tamil_parallel_en: நான் மாணவன் இல்லை "I am not a student" = 私は 学生じゃありません。 Here じゃありません is roughly "இல்லை / அல்ல" (not).
g01-2.formation_en: N1 + は + N2 + じゃありません (= ではありません)
g01-2.pitfalls_en: In talk, people also say 「じゃないです」. But in the exam, write じゃありません or ではありません. The は in ではありません is also read "wa".

g01-3.explanation_en: Add か at the end of a sentence to make it a question. You don’t need to change the word order. It is just like adding "-ஆ" in Tamil: "மாணவன்" (student) → "மாணவனா?" (student?). In Japanese you don’t need a question mark (?). か with 。 is enough. When you answer, start with はい (ஆமாம், yes) or いいえ (இல்லை, no). Then you can say a full sentence. ええ also means "yes". It is softer and used more in everyday talk than はい.
g01-3.tamil_parallel_en: நீங்கள் மாணவரா? — ஆமாம், மாணவன். "Are you a student? — Yes, I am a student." = あなたは 学生ですか。— はい、学生です。 Here か works like the Tamil question ending "-ஆ".
g01-3.formation_en: Sentence + か → はい、〜です / いいえ、〜じゃありません
g01-3.pitfalls_en: Make your voice go up on the か of a question. Don’t use あなた (you) too much. With someone you know, it is polite to use their name plus さん (田中さんは…).

g01-4.explanation_en: も means "too" or "also" (-உம், கூட). Say one thing is true about one person. If it is also true about another person, use も in place of は. Look at the Tamil "ராஜா மாணவன். நானும் மாணவன்." (Raja is a student. I am a student too.). The "-உம்" in "நானும்" is exactly も. It works the same way in "not" sentences. "I am not a doctor either" = 私も 医者じゃありません。 Note: when you use も, you don’t use は. In Tamil too, you don’t add another ending when you say "நானும்" (me too).
g01-4.tamil_parallel_en: ராஜா மாணவன். நானும் மாணவன். "Raja is a student. I am a student too." = ラジャさんは 学生です。私も 学生です。 Here も is the Tamil "-உம்" (too).
g01-4.formation_en: N + も + です / じゃありません (in place of は)
g01-4.pitfalls_en: A common mistake is to write は and も together, as in 「私はも」. も alone is enough. In English, "too" changes to "either" in "not" sentences. Japanese does not change the word. Just like Tamil, you keep using も.

g01-5.explanation_en: の joins two nouns together. In this lesson you use it to say where a person works or studies. 「IMCの 会社員」 = an IMC company worker (IMC நிறுவன ஊழியர்). 「IITマドラスの 学生」 = an IIT Madras student (IIT மதராஸ் மாணவர்). It is like the Tamil "-இன் / -உடைய" (of). It is also like just putting the two words side by side ("கல்லூரி மாணவர்", college student). The place name (N1) comes first. The person (N2) comes after. This order is exactly the same as Tamil ("TCS ஊழியர்" TCS employee, "அப்போலோ மருத்துவர்" Apollo doctor).
g01-5.tamil_parallel_en: நான் IIT மதராஸ் மாணவன் "I am an IIT Madras student" = 私は IITマドラスの 学生です。 Here の is roughly "-இன் / -ஐச் சேர்ந்த" (of / belonging to).
g01-5.pitfalls_en: Don’t flip the order like English "of". The Tamil order is right: place first, then person. Don’t use の twice, as in 「IMCのの会社員」.

g01-6.explanation_en: Put さん after another person’s name to be polite. It is the same for men and women. It is like Mr., Mrs. or Ms. It is like adding a word of respect in Tamil, as in "ராஜா அவர்கள்" (Raja sir) or "கவிதா அக்கா" (Kavitha akka). But never put さん after your own name: 「私は 田中です」. For small children and close female friends, use ちゃん. Put 人 (じん) after a country name to mean a person from that country. インド人 = Indian, 日本人 = Japanese. This is like Tamil "இந்திய-ர்" and "ஜப்பானிய-ர்". Put 歳 (さい) after a number to give an age. 五歳 (ごさい) = five years old. But note that some sounds change. 一歳 = いっさい, 八歳 = はっさい, 十歳 = じゅっさい.
g01-6.tamil_parallel_en: தனாகா அவர்கள் "Mr. Tanaka" / இந்திய-ர் "Indian" / ஐந்து வயது "five years old" = 田中さん / インド人 / 五歳. These Japanese endings go after the noun. The Tamil word of respect and the ending "-ர்" do the same.
g01-6.formation_en: Name + さん / ちゃん ; Country + 人(じん) ; Number + 歳(さい)
g01-6.pitfalls_en: Tamil speakers often put さん after their own name, as in 「私は ラジャさんです」. This is the most common mistake. 先生 (teacher) already shows respect by itself. You can say 「田中先生」. But don’t say 「田中先生さん」. 四歳 = よんさい (not しさい).

g01-7.explanation_en: To ask someone’s name, say 「お名前は？」. In Tamil you can ask "உங்கள் பெயர்?" (your name?) without finishing the sentence. Japanese is the same. You can drop 何ですか, stop at は and make your voice go up. お is a word you put in front to be polite. You will learn more about it in the next lesson. To ask "who?" politely, use どなた. The everyday word is 誰. You will learn it in the next lesson. To ask someone’s age, say 「何歳ですか」 (なんさい). To older people, the polite way is 「おいくつですか」. Numbers 0–10: ゼロ, いち, に, さん, し/よん, ご, ろく, しち/なな, はち, きゅう/く, じゅう. Tamil has only one word for each number. But Japanese has two ways to say 4, 7 and 9.
g01-7.tamil_parallel_en: உங்கள் பெயர்? "Your name?" / நீங்கள் யார்? "Who are you?" / எத்தனை வயது? "How old?" = お名前は？ / どなたですか / 何歳ですか
g01-7.formation_en: お名前は？ ; N は どなたですか ; N は 何歳ですか
g01-7.pitfalls_en: With people you have just met, use どなた. 誰 (だれ) is less polite. 何歳 = なんさい (not なにさい). Tamil says "உனக்கு எத்தனை வயது?" (how old are you?) with "-க்கு" (to you). But Japanese uses は here: 「〜さんは 何歳ですか」.

items.L01-q01: 学生 = がくせい (மாணவர், student). It ends with a long sound (せい). Making it short, as がくせ, is wrong. Also, the first sound is が, not か.
items.L01-q02: 先生 = せんせい (ஆசிரியர், teacher). Two common mistakes: changing the sound to ぜんせい, or making the long sound short as せんせ.
items.L01-q03: 医者 = いしゃ (மருத்துவர், doctor). しゃ is one sound, with a small ゃ. Reading it as two sounds, いしや, is wrong.
items.L01-q04: なまえ = 名前 (பெயர், name). 各 looks like 名, but it is a different character. 名 has the 夕 part on top.
items.L01-q05: きょうしつ = 教室 (வகுப்பறை, classroom). 数 looks like 教, but it is a different character. 至 is only the bottom part of 室.
items.L01-q06: When you meet someone for the first time, you start with はじめまして (nice to meet you). さようなら is what you say when you leave.
items.L01-q07: To say where someone is from, use country name + 人 (じん). インド人 = Indian (இந்தியர்). インド alone means the country India (இந்தியா).
items.L01-q08: To say an age, use number + 歳 (さい). 五歳 = five years old (ஐந்து வயது). じん means a person from a country. さん is the polite word after a name.
items.L01-q09: To ask "Who are you?" politely, use どなた (யார், who). The answer is a name, "Tanaka". So only a "who" question fits.
items.L01-q10: The answer says "not a student". So it must start with いいえ (இல்லை, no). はい and ええ both mean "yes" (ஆமாம்).
items.L01-q11: A person who has come from India to study is a 留学生 (வெளிநாட்டு மாணவர், international student). きょうしつ (வகுப்பறை, classroom) and くに (நாடு, country) are not people.
items.L01-q12: "Not a doctor, a teacher" means "Raja-san is a teacher" (ஆசிரியர்). The first choice gives the job that the sentence said "not" to.
items.L01-q13: も = "too" (-உம்). "Yamada-san is Japanese too" means "Yamada-san is Japanese". 外国人 (வெளிநாட்டவர், foreigner) means the opposite.
items.L01-q14: インド人 = an Indian (இந்திய நாட்டவர்). So it means "Raja-san’s country is India". "A teacher from India" adds a job. The sentence does not say that.
items.L01-q15: Use は to show the topic: 私は カビタです = I am Kavitha. This is the first sentence of the introduction. Nothing comes before it, so you can’t say "me too" (も).
items.L01-q16: What the last sentence said is also true for this person. So "too" (-உம்) = も. は is not wrong, but you lose the meaning "also". The JLPT wants も.
items.L01-q17: The reply is はい, so the first sentence is a question. A question ends with か (like Tamil "-ஆ"). は and も don’t come at the end of a sentence.
items.L01-q18: Join the place and the person with の: IITマドラスの 学生 = an IIT Madras student (IIT மதராஸ் மாணவர்). は is not used twice in one sentence.
items.L01-q19: The next sentence says "student". So the first sentence must say "not a teacher" = じゃありません. です would say "a teacher, a student". That does not make sense.
items.L01-q20: A reply that starts with いいえ says "no". So it needs じゃありません. If you say いいえ and then end with です, the two parts don’t agree.
items.L01-q21: Stop at は in 「お名前は？」 and make your voice go up. This asks "Your name?" (உங்கள் பெயர்?). か does not come right after a noun here. This is a short form of 「お名前は 何ですか」.
items.L01-q22: 私は インドの 留学生です。 — topic (私は) → の joins (インドの) → noun (留学生) → です. 留学生 goes in the ★ slot.
items.L01-q23: 田中さんも 日本語教室の 先生です。 — first the topic with も, then the の phrase, then 先生です. 日本語教室の goes in the ★ slot.
items.L01-q24: 山田先生は どなたですか。 — the question word どなた comes before です. か comes last. どなた goes in the ★ slot.
items.L01-q25: ［1］ Country + 人 = Indian (இந்தியர்). ［2］ Kavitha is a student, and Tanaka-san is a student too. So use も. ［3］ The text says "student", so "not a teacher" uses じゃありません.
